scope: D3D9 additional buffer binding references join standalone/implicit private binding_refs. Physical chain/backing/view storage remains until chain public, surface public and binding counts are all zero. Surface/chain public counts each hold exactly one parent pin on positive-count edges; internal bindings own no public parent pins. Last internal unbind can retire an unreferenced additional chain, while a public chain or surface keeps storage alive. Physical chain destruction unlinks first, emits DestroySwapChain, detaches association and calls the storage destructor directly; remove the obsolete device_pin_transferred flag and synthetic public surface Release. Reset does not deduct private slots from public counts; public chains or views block, binding-only chains allow Reset. Native actual public/storage/device/private methods add 2603 checks, 640 explicit surface/chain revivals across two internal slots and five final-owner orders; old source strictly compiles and fails public-counter assertion. SDK XP uses full setters/getters/GetContainer/QueryInterface, 32 surface and 32 container loop revivals plus two frame-chain revivals and two public Reset-blocker revivals; two true-four-sample Clear/chain-Present frames, binding-only Reset, no-public final device and last-unbind paths. Three protected private finalizers query device count one. XP is proxy execution; pixel replay separately verifies real four-sample attachment, raw resolved and displayed buffers. No native Microsoft HAL/game/FPS claims, other texture/cube/buffer/shader/state-block binding public counts, general root-device state preservation with external children, arbitrary reentrant/thread/device-loss graphs, full Reset/private-cache boundaries, formats/MSAA/fullscreen/multiple-buffer rotation or review stages 4/5/6 completion. D3D8/DDraw, host/protocol/shader/bundle unchanged.

sources.evidence: Supporting standalone/public device-pin edges, internal target-view binding and public getters. The bridge extends internal binding storage to additional buffers; public zero chain/surface recovery and finalizer safety are implementation invariants exercised here, not a new original Microsoft HAL run.
